subject: Introducing uncertainty into animal indentification during transects

messages.author: b4370a397bda3bc4
messages.subject: Introducing uncertainty into animal indentification during transects
parts:
Hi all,

I have been working on putting together some Distance sampling and DSMs on a foraging ground used by Green Turtles in the Florida Keys, and I have come across a possibly unique problem when looking at the data.  These grounds have two size classes that use the foraging grounds, these size classes are usually delineated by the length of the shell, (< 85 cm is a sub-adult, > 85cm is a adult) when the animals is captured.  Something we do not do during our transect surveys, so there exists some uncertainty when we are identifying green turtles by size class during our transect surveys.

However, once transect surveys are done we do capture animals on these foraging grounds, and when we do we can look at what our initial call of size class when the animal was sighted before capture, and then what the subsequent shell measurement tells us the size class actually was.  Through this, we know we are correct about 80% of the time.  Is there a way to incorporate this uncertainty into the modelling?

TL/DR: When identifying animals to size class during surveys we know there is about a 20% chance there is mis-identification happening, is it possible to incorporate this into Distance?

thanks,
Ryan

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Introducing uncertainty into animal indentification during transects
parts:
Ryan

This form of mis-identification is handled by something called the "Multi-Analysis Engine" or mads.  You can read about it in Chapter 12 of the Distance for Windows users guide, or download the `mads` package from CRAN if you are using R.  You can read some short lecture notes here

https://workshops.distancesampling.org/standrews-2019/adv/slides/mads.pdf

Unfortunately the mads methodology does not at present feed into the dsm modelling framework.
